title: Solids, Liquids and Changes of State
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Solids, Liquids and Changes of State Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Compare the properties of solids and liquids and describe how adding or removing heat causes a change of state between solid and liquid (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on solids and liquids, melting and freezing, and melting points, with examples such as icy poles, chocolate and candle wax. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Solids keep their shape, liquids flow; adding or removing heat changes one into the other.
body_html:
How to think about it

Solids keep their own shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.

  • Adding heat can melt a solid into a liquid (ice, chocolate, butter, wax).
  • Removing heat can freeze a liquid into a solid. Water freezes and ice melts at 0 °C.
  • Melting and freezing are reversible: the material stays the same, only its state changes.
Example

An icy pole drips in the sun. Which change?

heat is added

solid to liquid

Answer: melting

Example

Is sand a solid?

each grain keeps its shape

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sand or sugar is a liquid because it can be poured.
  • Thinking ice disappears when it melts.
  • Thinking freezing needs a freezer (water freezes at 0 °C wherever it is that cold).

faq.q: What is the difference between a solid and a liquid?
faq.a: A solid keeps its own shape. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container, but the amount stays the same.
It is the temperature at which a solid melts. Ice melts at 0 °C; chocolate melts at about 30–35 °C.
Yes. When a melted solid cools, it can become solid again, like melted chocolate setting on a cake.
